data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A structurally novel 13-input sorting network of 45 or fewer comparators can be constructed by identifying and iteratively pruning redundant comparators from Batcher's odd-even mergesort network, which initially requires 48 comparators.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If Batcher's 48-comparator network for n=13 is strictly irreducible (every comparator is necessary for at least one of the 8192 binary input vectors), then the pruning strategy yields a 48-comparator network and fails to find a 45-comparator candidate.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the iterative pruning process converges to a local minimum of 46 or 47 comparators, the specific structural hypothesis fails to achieve the 45-comparator target.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Generate the comparator list for Batcher's odd-even mergesort on 13 inputs (48 comparators). Using the 0-1 principle, a sandboxed Python simulation will evaluate all 8192 binary vectors to identify redundant comparators. For each comparator in the network, the simulation temporarily removes it and checks if the 0-1 sorting property is preserved. If the property is preserved, the comparator is permanently pruned. Iteratively passing through the network until no more redundant comparators are found yields a smaller, structurally novel network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
